clean_builder_reconfirmation.description: Post-hoc code review (07.3-REVIEW.md) found 2 blocker-level bugs in tests/nl2sparql/eval/grounding_index_builder.py used to build the grounding index that produced the numbers above: CR-01 (no filter excluding ontology-level owl:Class/owl:ObjectProperty/owl:DatatypeProperty subjects, so 45/2618 indexed 'entities' were schema terms retrievable by 43/49 (88%) of CK25 questions) and CR-02 (label literal-stripping stripped quotes before splitting the '^^'/'@lang' suffix, corrupting every language-tagged label, e.g. 'has manager"@en' instead of 'has manager'). Both fixed (commits f932360 CR-01, 6c72b37 CR-02; index 2618->2573 entities, schema IRIs excluded, zero stray-quote labels remain, offline recall guard unchanged at 0.96) and the full grounded-vs-fresh-zero same-session sweep was re-run on the corrected builder.
clean_builder_reconfirmation.result: Aggregate reproduces IDENTICALLY on the clean builder (14/49 vs 5/49, b=9/c=0/p=0.0039, paired_delta=0.1837, ci_95=[0.0816, 0.3061]) -- but the gained-case SET shifted: pre-fix gained ck25-9 and ck25-46; clean-builder gained ck25-10 and ck25-11 instead (both sets still 9 cases, still zero regressions). The `cases`/`gained_0_to_1` fields above have been updated in place to the clean-builder values, superseding the pre-fix per-case data.
clean_builder_reconfirmation.interpretation: Removing the schema-IRI noise (CR-01) and the label corruption (CR-02) did NOT inflate or manufacture the measured lift -- the identical aggregate on a demonstrably cleaner index is stronger evidence for the NL-ACC-01 significant-lift disposition, not weaker.

openai-gpt4o-mini-ck25-grounded.note: Second real execution-graded CK25 live accuracy number (Plan 07.3-06): gpt-4o-mini-generated SPARQL with entity/instance grounding (Seam 6 -- retrieved instance IRIs+labels for named entities injected into the prompt so the model binds to real IRIs instead of inventing them) judged via answer-set execution against the vendored CK25 instance graph (judge: execution, same as scripted-ck25/openai-gpt4o-mini-ck25). Per-case `judge_note` D-05 buckets (candidate_engine_rejected / gold_engine_limitation) were NOT captured in this sweep's paste-back (only name/passed/elapsed_ms per case) -- a documented limitation, not a fabricated zero; a future re-sweep could capture judge_note for a finer failure breakdown. UPDATED post-review: code review (07.3-REVIEW.md) found 2 blockers (CR-01 schema-IRI leakage, CR-02 label corruption) in the eval's grounding_index_builder.py; both fixed (commits f932360/6c72b37) and this sweep re-run in full on the corrected builder. The `cases` map and `confirmatory_test.gained_0_to_1` above are the CORRECTED-builder values (superseding the pre-fix per-case data); see `confirmatory_test.clean_builder_reconfirmation` for the full before/after comparison. Combined with the standalone arm's non-significant-but-worse point estimate above (configs.openai-gpt4o-mini-ck25-predicate-grounded.confirmatory_test, p=0.1250), seam-7 predicate/schema-convention grounding gives no execution-graded CK25 lift, standalone or additive, once the full schema is genuinely surfaced. Notably 2 genuine additive wins (ck25-8, ck25-11) show real case-level signal, offset by 4 distraction losses -- consistent with a schema-info-overload hypothesis rather than the predicate index being simply useless. CLOSED via the DOCUMENTED-NULL path (NL-FEW-02 precedent) on a now-VALID experiment -- NEVER as a passed confirmatory lift. qald9plus_directional.description: Directional-only generalization check (RESEARCH D-03), explicitly NOT a gate: first-ever live QALD-9-plus run, zero-shot vs predicate-grounded, both gpt-4o-mini.
qald9plus_directional.note: Both arms sit at the floor (1/514 and 3/514) -- a +2-case delta is well inside the ~5.5-6.2pt achieved MDE at n=514, i.e. noise, not a signal; not a gate per D-03/D-04 in any case. QALD-9-plus gold data contains a malformed date literal ('YYYY-10-31') that causes non-fatal rdflib parse warnings during the run; both runs completed and produced these pass_rates despite the warnings. Recorded as D-04's honest generalization ceiling for seam-7 on a non-corporate, DBpedia-domain benchmark -- never blended with the CK25 numbers above (RESEARCH Pitfall 3). CR-01 note (07.4-06 re-fold): QALD-9-plus predicate grounding runs in RETRIEVE mode (k=20, well under PREDICATE_DUMP_THRESHOLD's dump-mode path), so it was never affected by the CR-01 dump-mode defect; these numbers are unchanged and were not re-run.

key_findings: VALID RE-RUN (07.4-06 re-fold, post CR-01 dump-mode fix, pin b66932046a102898e8fff205a7ddcbedfb2c896e): with the full CK25 schema now genuinely dumped, seam-7 predicate/schema-convention grounding STILL gives no execution-graded CK25 lift over entity-grounding: standalone it is a non-significant worse point estimate (7/49 vs a fresh 12/49 entity-alone arm, McNemar p=0.1250, 1 gain/6 losses), and additively composed on top of entity-grounding (the phase's actual intended composition) it is a non-significant wash with a slightly lower point estimate (10/49 vs 12/49, p=0.6875, 2 gains/4 losses).

2 genuine additive wins (ck25-8, ck25-11) show real case-level signal from predicate grounding, offset by 4 distraction losses (ck25-6, ck25-12, ck25-30, ck25-49) -- the mechanically-derived predicate index helps on some cases but net-hurts via distraction once the full schema is dumped, not simply irrelevant.

SUPERSEDES the 07.4-05 confounded findings: the prior standalone arm was WRONG-DIRECTION SIGNIFICANT (5/49 vs 12/49, p=0.0156) and the prior additive arm was an exact-tie wash (13/49 vs 13/49, p=1.0) -- both measured against a dump mode that only ever surfaced 1-8 of 30 predicates. The valid re-run changes the standalone arm from significant-regression to non-significant-null, and leaves the additive arm a documented null either way -- the overall NL-ACC-02 disposition (fails the hard gate, closes via documented-null) is UNCHANGED, but is now resting on a valid experiment instead of a confounded one.

Documented follow-up (not this phase): predicate grounding shows case-level signal (real wins on ck25-8/ck25-11) but nets ~zero-to-negative due to distraction losses; the next experiment should try SELECTIVE predicate surfacing (only predicates relevant to the question's target class) rather than a full dump or naive token-match retrieval.

QALD-9-plus directional generalization is at the floor for BOTH arms (1/514, 3/514) -- too small a delta to interpret against the ~5.5-6.2pt achieved MDE; unaffected by the CR-01 fix (QALD runs in retrieve mode, k=20, never in the dump-mode path) and not re-run this session.
limitations: The additive-arm comparison now HAS full per-case verdict dicts for both the fresh entity-alone arm and the additive arm (captured this re-fold, session 3) -- an improvement over the 07.4-05 aggregate-only capture. Both QALD-9-plus comparisons still captured only aggregate pass-rates (unchanged, not re-run this session).

The standalone predicate-alone arm's re-run (session 3) and the additive arm's re-run (also session 3) now share a SINGLE fresh entity-alone arm (12/49) run once in the same session and paired against both -- a methodological improvement over 07.4-05, which used two different sessions (12/49 session 1, 13/49 session 2) for the two comparisons.

shape_coverage.metric: 100% of held-out failing cases' shape TYPES are present in the generated bank's 9-shape repertoire (coarse shape-type reading: does at least one bank example share the failing case's shape category).
shape_coverage.metric_caveat: 07.5-SPEC.md's shape-coverage metric is underspecified between two readings: (a) coarse shape-TYPE membership (used above, 100%) vs (b) literal canonical-skeleton equality (the exact _skeleton() abstraction test_fewshot_bank_disjoint.py uses for the overlap audit). The literal skeleton reading yields a DEGENERATE 0%, because the generated bank's skeletons are near-disjoint from the corpus's gold skeletons BY DESIGN -- that disjointness IS the overlap-exclusion axis (D-05); a generated example structurally identical to a held-out gold would be a leaked near-duplicate, not a coverage win. Recording the coarse shape-type reading (100%, clears REQ-6's >=70% bar) and this caveat explicitly, rather than reporting the literal-skeleton 0% without context or silently picking whichever reading clears the bar.

faithfulness.requirement: REQ-3 secondary: >=20-pair LLM-judge faithfulness audit on the REGENERATED bank

faithfulness.instrument_reliability_finding: The gpt-4o-mini judge is an UNRELIABLE instrument for this task: manual domain/range adjudication of every judge-flagged NO in each run found >=2 provable false-negatives per run -- cases where the judge said NO on a query that correctly answers the question once the schema's implicit domain/range typing is accounted for (the judge does not reliably reason about implicit-domain grouped-aggregation queries even when given domain/range context in the prompt). Manual domain/range adjudication of the same pairs put TRUE faithfulness at approximately 88%-96%.
faithfulness.disposition: DOCUMENTED-PARTIAL, not a clean pass. The specified gpt-4o-mini faithfulness judge cannot reliably certify REQ-3's >=95% judge-match bar (it false-negatives provably-correct implicit-domain grouped-aggregation queries even with domain/range context supplied). Paraphrases -- the artifact the judge evaluates -- are unused by the capability under test (FewShotIndex reads only question+query, never paraphrases), so this gap does not affect the CK25/QALD lift measurement itself. Recorded honestly as documented-partial rather than reframed as a pass.

key_findings: The generated (mechanically synthesized, never hand-curated) CK25 few-shot bank reproduces Spike 001's directional lift: a statistically significant paired McNemar result (p<0.05) on all 3 independent same-session runs, both raw and after excluding the one shape+entity-overlap-audited near-duplicate case (ck25-4).

The lift survives overlap exclusion essentially unchanged (raw and overlap-excluded deltas differ by <0.5pt on every run), confirming the measured lift is not an artifact of bank<->corpus near-duplication.

ck25-50 is a known-flaky single-case regression (typo'd compound top-N+count question), present in 2 of 3 runs but not systematic -- b (gains) exceeds c (regressions) by a wide margin on every run (10:1, 9:1, 8:0).

QALD-9-plus generalization is a non-issue this phase by construction: the generated QALD bank is honestly empty (D-04, no synthesizable shapes survived QALD's structural-only TBox), so the generated-fewshot arm IS the zero-shot arm -- non-regression is trivially satisfied, not a generalization finding.

The specified faithfulness judge (gpt-4o-mini) is not a reliable REQ-3 certification instrument: it produces provable false-negatives on correct implicit-domain grouped-aggregation queries. Manual domain/range adjudication estimates true faithfulness at 88-96%, below the naive judge's own 76-84% raw scores -- the judge under-reports faithfulness, it does not over-report it.
limitations: Full 49-case per-case verdict dicts were captured only for run 3 (the run written to generated_sweep_result.json on disk); runs 1-2 are recorded as aggregate pass counts + b/c/p/delta + gains/regressions case-name lists, pasted back by the human rather than machine-captured. This mirrors the phase07_dense_few_shot_sweep precedent for the same reason (avoiding a fabricated per-case dict).

The 3-run sweep predates the two_hop NL-question faithfulness fix (commit 20f40a0); see bank_provenance.two_hop_nl_fix_provenance_caveat for why a re-sweep was judged unnecessary (query text, the actual lever, is unchanged).

This sweep is recorded here as a sibling top-level key (not promoted to a configs['openai-gpt4o-mini-ck25-generated-fewshot'] BaselineConfig entry) for the same reason as phase07_dense_few_shot_sweep/phase07_4_predicate_grounding_sweep: BaselineConfig.cases requires a full per-case dict, which is only available for run 3 of 3.
